related_questions.question: What is the role of GSH in cancer patients?
related_questions.snippet: Hence, GSH has both protective and pathogenic roles. Although in healthy cells it is crucial for the removal and detoxification of carcinogens, elevated GSH levels in tumor cells are associated with tumor progression and increased resistance to chemotherapeutic drugs.
related_questions.title: Role of Glutathione in Cancer: From Mechanisms to Therapies - PMC

related_questions.question: Is glycolysis a possible target for cancer treatment?
related_questions.snippet: The enhanced glycolysis in the cancer cells correlates with an upregulation and activation of critical glycolytic enzymes. Targeting the key glycolytic enzymes is a promising strategy to rewire the altered tumor metabolism, to sensitize (or re-sensitize, when resistance develops) cancers to chemotherapy.
related_questions.title: Modulating Glycolysis to Improve Cancer Therapy - MDPI

related_questions.question: Why are some glycolysis inhibitors being studied as anti-cancer treatments?
related_questions.snippet: Many of the key effectors of glycolysis (enzymes and transporters) can be considered as promising targets for therapeutic intervention against cancer. Some of them are overexpressed in invasive tumors and, therefore, offer a relatively safe therapeutic window for anticancer agents that target them.
related_questions.title: Anti-cancer agents counteracting tumor glycolysis - PubMed Central

related_questions.question: What is the target enzyme for cancer chemotherapy?
related_questions.snippet: Thymidylate synthase (TS) is a key enzyme in the synthesis of 2′-deoxythymidine-5′-monophosphate, an essential precursor for DNA biosynthesis. For this reason, this enzyme is a critical target in cancer chemotherapy.
